key_insight: This paper shows that in Mixture-of-Experts reinforcement learning, expert routing is not just an internal implementation detail—it can be actively explored to create more diverse rollouts and improve learning. In other words, changing which experts are selected can help the model discover better training signals.
problem_solved: Prior MoE-RL methods mainly focused on stabilizing optimization and improving efficiency, while treating expert selection as fixed. This paper addresses the missed opportunity of using routing itself as a controllable source of rollout diversity in RL.
method: Empirically analyze how perturbing expert routing changes rollout behavior and output distributions.
Treat expert selection as an exploration dimension during reinforcement learning rather than a fixed sparse computation path.
Leverage expert-space exploration to increase diversity in sampled trajectories and potentially improve post-training outcomes.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a new lever for improving MoE RL beyond loss design and optimizer tuning. It provides a practical direction for making sparse models explore more effectively during post-training, which may lead to better performance and more robust policy learning.

paper_title: Expert-Space Exploration in MoE Reinforcement Learning
paper_authors: Hongyi He, Zhenghao Lin, Xiao Liu, Peng Cheng, Yan Lu
